record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: If X is an exotic C^n, must the action of its algebraic automorphism group Aut(X) on X fail to be transitive? Likewise, must the action of the group of analytic automorphisms fail to be transitive?

evidence.quote:

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a smooth complex affine algebraic variety $X$ of dimension $n$ that is diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$ but not algebraically isomorphic to the affine space $\mathbb{C}^n$. Let $\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ denote the group of algebraic automorphisms of $X$, and let $\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{hol}}(X)$ denote the group of biholomorphic (analytic) automorphisms of $X$.

(a) Prove or disprove: for every exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$, the natural action of $\mathrm{Aut}(X)$ on $X$ is not transitive.

(b) Prove or disprove: for every exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$, the natural action of $\mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{hol}}(X)$ on $X$ is not transitive.
artifact.category_tag: Automorphism groups of exotic affine spaces
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Kaliman and Zaidenberg constructs contractible smooth affine varieties non-isomorphic to Euclidean spaces with very (in fact infinitely) transitive automorphism group actions on the smooth locus, and the theory of flexibility/infinite transitivity has developed substantially. However, it is not clear from available sources whether any such examples are bona fide exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ (diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{R}^{2n}$), nor whether the original transitivity questions for both algebraic and analytic automorphism groups of exotic $\mathbb{C}^n$ have been settled. The status appears to remain unresolved in the literature accessible via search.

status_evidence.title: Affine modifications and affine hypersurfaces with a very transitive automorphism group
status_evidence.snippet: Applies affine modifications to construct contractible smooth affine varieties non-isomorphic to Euclidean spaces, with automorphism groups acting m-transitively on the smooth part.
status_evidence.claim: Provides constructions of contractible affine varieties with very transitive automorphism groups, relevant to but not clearly resolving the exotic C^n transitivity question.

status_evidence.title: Infinite transitivity and special automorphisms
status_evidence.snippet: Develops the theory of flexible varieties and infinite transitivity of the special automorphism group.
status_evidence.claim: Modern theory of transitivity for affine variety automorphism groups, with no explicit resolution of the exotic C^n case.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of affine varieties and their Lie algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Recent overview by Kraft and Zaidenberg of automorphism groups of affine varieties, including open problems.
status_evidence.claim: Recent surveys still treat transitivity questions in this area as active, suggesting the specific question for exotic C^n is not definitively settled.
